profile_text.body:
The Allen Institute for AI, known as Ai2, is a nonprofit AI research organization founded in 2014 by Paul Allen and headquartered in Seattle, WA. Led by Ali Farhadi, the institute describes itself as conducting high-impact research and engineering to tackle key problems in artificial intelligence, guided by open, collaborative, and inclusive principles aimed at producing safe, ethical, and trustworthy AI systems. The organization maintains research partnerships with the University of Washington's Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science and Engineering, the National Science Foundation on an open multimodal AI infrastructure project, and Google Cloud for model and platform development.

Ai2's work spans foundational AI research as well as applied domains including climate science, agriculture and food security, wildfire management, and wildlife protection. The institute produces two tracked AI products: OLMo, an open-source language model developed with fully open training data and an emphasis on research transparency, and Semantic Scholar, an academic search tool that provides paper summaries and citation graphs for the research community. Both products reflect the institute's nonprofit, open-science orientation.

The held facts note no litigation or regulatory filings associated with Ai2, and no MCP server presence has been recorded. The organization's profile is verified as of August 2026.
